properties.Name: Seneca Theatre
properties.Statement: A large, illuminated marquee was part of the original facade, the upper part of which still exhibits Art Deco styling. The interior was decorated throughout with Native Seneca motifs such as birchbark-cast plaster walls, ceremonial masks and belt designs. The theatre floor was graded to give each of the original 918 seats a front row view of the screen.  A mural on the upper interior walls was one of the last commissions of Montreal-based  theatrical decorator and artist Emmanuel Briffa. The theatre (c. 1940), originally owned by Famous Players Theatre was designed by Jay I. English. Hosted many events over the years, including the Canadian premiere of Marilyn Monroe's film "Niagara" on January 28 1953.

properties.Name: Drew Stone Cottage
properties.Statement: This house (c.1857) is an excellent example of the vernacular Ontario Cottage style popular circa 1830-1870. Its facade is built of cut limestone blocks with raised quoins, and door and window surrounds of sandstone blocks; its other walls are of coursed rubble construction the rear wings and front portico were turn of the century additions. One of the earliest surviving houses built in the old town of Clifton, it was the first home of John Drew (1833-1914), a mason from Devonshire. He would become one of the town's most prolific contractors, erecting a number of substantial homes and public buildings including the old Town Hall and Glenview Mansion.

properties.Name: Chippawa Town Hall
properties.Statement: The building (c. 1842) exhibits a commercial Greek Revival style of the 1840's. It bears such rectilinear details as heavy granite pilasters with doric capitals, a frieze above the storefront, quoining and heavy windowsills. The other walls are of coursed rubble construction. Its facade is the only original one left around the old town square. Initially a general store owned by Hugh Fraser and Douglas Stephenson, the building was bought by the Town Council after 1851. The ground floor was rented out to retailers, while the Town offices occupied the upper floor until 1970. The second floor was also rented out for various social and religious gatherings.
properties.Attributes: 2 storey Classical Revival building; symmetrical three-bay ashlar stone façade; four-sided mansard roof with a clock tower was a later addition; two over two sash windows found along the front and side facades; heavy limestone quoins, sills and lintel surrounds on the south facade; four limestone pilasters with Doric capitals; two large single pane windows found between pilasters on front; unornamented frieze with a simple cornice separating the first and second storeys

properties.Name: Woodruff Block
properties.Statement: Block was built by Joseph C. Woodruff (c. 1857-58) in the early Italianate style with narrow windows, decorative labels and ornate roof brackets. The Woodruff's were one of the longest established families in the Niagara area.  While he held a tavern license in Drummondville and a store on Main Street, he rented the building rather than using it himself.  The property had a general store, post office (until it relocated), and brokerage offices.  In later years, it held the Princess Theatre which was the first movie and vaudeville theatre in Niagara Falls (1908-1914) and the Maple Leaf Restaurant and Bakery (1922-1932). In 1933, it opened as the Empire Hotel and became the Empire Tavern in 1949 until it closed in 1993.

properties.Name: Peter McGarry House
properties.Statement: c. 1840. Original owner listed as McGarry.

properties.Name: Orchard-Cadham House
properties.Statement: This house (c. 1850) represents a style in transition, initially a classically designed house, that has been altered.  Corinthian pilasters are still evident at the back corner.  It has many features of the Queen Anne Revival style.  The house features both decorative and wood shingle finish and clapboard siding which was often used to embellish the architecture of the late Victorian period. The tower and verandah were probably added later in the 1890's.  John Allen Orchard who owned this house was a prominent member of the Drummondville and Stamford communities.   He came with his father from England in 1836. He purchased Lot 5 on Culp Street in 1856.  The house would have been built soon after.  He served as township clerk and clerk of the division court. His nephew Joseph Cadham lived there after his uncle's death in 1896.  Joseph's daughter Margaret inherited the house and lived there the rest of her life.
properties.Attributes: Rectilinear plan in east-west direction with circular tower at south east corner; main house is one and a half storeys with a steeply pitched gable roof; rear is lower one and a half storey tail with gable roof; roof is steeply pitched gable with decorative wood shingle tympanum at highest part of each gable; balbe has two windows (2 x 2 sash); decorative moulding applied to vergeboard of gable ends; the walls have slight flare and the tower has wood shingles; one over one sash windows; there is a large round headed window to west (left) of front door which retains its leaded stain glass transom in half round upper portion;  Front door is wooden with top 1/3 being glass and lower 2/3 consisting of 9 small panels 3 x 3; ornate door knob, plate and doorbell; large red chimney is on the east side; open veranda extends across front facade west of tower with four plain Doric columns providing support and dentil moulding under the eave of the porch roof and along the porch entablature; limestone foundation; (refer to by-law for full details).

properties.Name: Mitchell Cottage
properties.Statement: The house (c. 1850) was constructed as a log cabin (smaller than the present structure) with heavy timber beams and a stone foundation. In the 1840's, an extension was built on the south end, and Classical Revival elements such as eave returns and a "Georgian wilderness" type door were added. The exterior is covered with stucco. Also known as Stamford Cottage, the original cabin was built on Crown land granted to the Presbyterian Church to assist early settlers.  The original owner of the house is considered to be John Mitchell.  It was later owned by John Hawkins from 1837 to 1853, and it is to him that the 1840's appearance of the house is attributed. The designation bylaw was partially repealed in 1996.
properties.Attributes: The only known log structure remaining in the City; one and a half storey with an asymmetrical four bay façade; first storey is white stucco while the top half storey is clad in clapboard; rectangular form with an inverted north east corner; medium-pitch gable roof with plain eave trim and eave returns; north facade is a typical gable end; south facade gable end has the rake extending further towards the east; eaves extend from the south facade gable along the east facade to the centre of the house, which creates an unusual roof structure; two inset brick chimneys located on either side of the structure; centred front door case containing a "Georgian Wilderness" style opening, if a size panel door, two recessed 5-light panels and four pilasters with Doric capitals; a pair of 6 over 6 sash with plain surrounds on the north west facade; single 12 over 12 sash with the plain surround on the south west and south facades; double hung sash windows in the north and south facades; connection to the Stamford Presbyterian Church and the history of the Stamford Township

properties.Name: Morse & Sons Funeral Home
properties.Statement: Original building was constructed in 1826--present building is more recent.  Was the site of a furniture maker prior to becoming a Funeral Home.

properties.Name: Willoughby Township Hall
properties.Statement: With its small size and simplified Classical Revival styling, the hall (c. 1877), built by David Morningstar, represents the type of rural public buildings found in late 19th century Ontario. Renovation in 1966 resulted in the removal of an original round front gable window and fanlight over the entrance and the covering of the exterior clapboard with asbestos siding. The hall was the first permanent meeting place for the Township of Willoughby's political body. It was used for church and social programs, concerts and exhibitions. When the Township was joined with Niagara Falls in 1970, the hall became a community centre.
properties.Attributes: One storey civic building with a symmetrical three bay façade; exterior asbestos siding, a replacement of the original clapboard exterior; medium-pitch roof clad in asphalt shingles, likely a replacement of the original wood shingles; round headed window on either side of a central doorway on the east (front) facade; round-headed 4 over 4 sash windows with plain sills; two windows on the east (front) facade, three windows on the north facade and two on the south facade (originally three); location of many community group activities; strong significance to the history and development of the Wiloughby Township and several of its key political figures

properties.Name: Stamford Township Hall
properties.Statement: The hall (c. 1874) with its durable hammer dressed limestone construction, has changed little over the years. Its eclectic Italianate styling includes a gabled hip roof with brackets and gingerbread trim, windows of different shape on the first and second storeys, and the main entrance archway with a keystone and voussoirs. Designed by noted local architect John Latshaw, and built by Dutton and Brown the hall was Stamford's political centre from 1874 to 1963. The basement was leased by the Drummondville fire department until 1913. In 1970, the building became the Lundy's Lane Historical Museum. In 2009, during the planning for the new addition, the museum will become known as the Niagara Falls History Museum.
properties.Attributes: Two storey rectangular structure with a symmetrical, three bay façade; exterior of limestone with ribbon pointing; built in the Italianate style popular in the third quarter of the 19th century; the building has a projected  band of ashlar masonry between the foundation and the exterior walls; hip roof with gables on the north (front) and south (rear); roof is made of cedar shingles, a 1981 alteration from the original terne-plate roof and replaced during the 2010/2011 restoration/renovation; roof features decorative brackets and wooden dentils; small gingerbread feature in each gable; central front entrance which features a transom and semi-circular window; segmental stone arch with keystone above the entrance, with a date stone just above; double-hung, 4 over 4 sash with segmental arched openings, the east and west facade windows have limestone surrounds; two windows similar to a Florentine window located on the north (front) facade, flanked by two round-headed openings with stone voussoirs; east facade basement level features a set of large wood doors under a segmental stone arch; Queen Victoria Memoria Fountain placed on the north east corner of the property, previously set on the north west corner having been moved from Main and Ferry; connected to noted architect John Latshaw, who had designed multiple civic buildings in the Niagara area; assists in understanding the history and development of the Township of Stamford and the City of Niagara Falls

properties.Name: Niagara Falls Armoury
properties.Statement: The Armoury was built (c. 1911) in the style of a late Medieval fortress. It features simulated defense towers at the corners, a crenellated parapet and a massive front entrance formed by a Tudor Gothic arch. The red brick facade has limestone detailing such as windowsills surrounds capping and corbels now covered by paint. It was designed by T. W. Fuller, a government military architect and son of Thomas Fuller who designed the old post office and built by Alonzo Robertson. It was one of 11 armouries built during a period of reform and expansion in the Canadian militia (1896-1911) and was a recruitment and training centre during the First World War.
properties.Attributes: Constructed of red brick laid in common bond and quarry-faced limestone; massive front entrance and triple Tudor Gothic arch; north tower whose size and decorative treatments make it the focal point; crenellated parapet with limestone accents; stone corbels across the front and side facades; buttresses around the structure; tall 1 over 1 sash with plain limestone sills on the first storey; paired sets of 1 over 1 sash with square transoms, limestone sill and lintel, and a matching limestone mullion in between on the second storey; a recessed stone crest found on the north tower; date stone above the entranceway, reading "19 Armoury 11"; large field gun on the corner of the property, captured from German forces of Kaiser Wilhelm at the Battle of Amiens in 1918; one of eleven drill halls built in Ontario between 1896 and 1918 and a testament to the development of the Volunteer Militia; association with military architect T.W.Fuller; constructed by local Robertson Construction Company

properties.Name: Willoughby Manor
properties.Statement: The facade of this impressive house (c.1835) is dominated by a two-storey Classical style portico which features fluted columns with ionic capitals, entablatures at both levels and a barrel roof with a closed semicircular pediment. Inside, the original curved staircase remains although a ballroom once located on the second floor has been lost. James Cummings, born in 1789, was the son of Thomas Cummings, the first settler in Chippawa. A successful merchant, he fought in the War of 1812 and became active in politics, serving as reeve, justice of the peace and member of the legislature. He was also one of the incorporators of the Erie and Ontario Railroad in 1835.

properties.Name: Crompton House
properties.Statement: Built in the Classical Revival Style it has a symmetrical façade with a front door flanked with transom windows.  The first floor windows are double hung.  The verandah is across the whole front façade and it has Doric order columns.  There is a medium pitched gable roof with two dormers that were later additions.  The Crompton family owned the property for a long time.

properties.Name: Old Imperial Bank
properties.Statement: The bank is an eclectic blend of Romanesque Revival and French Renaissance styles (c. 1906). Its massive limestone construction, with details such as carved door lintels and block window surrounds, gives the  impression of strength and security. It was designed by the well-known Toronto firm of Darling and Pearson.  It was a branch of the Imperial Bank (later the CIBC) from 1906 until 1967. The bank gained nationwide attention in March 1964, when thieves cut their way into the vault in the southeast corner of the bank from an adjacent building. The robbers briefly netted themselves over $900,000 before their capture three weeks later.
properties.Attributes: Two and 1/2 storey rectangular structure with a symmetrical three bay façade; connection to the architectural firm of Darling and Pearson; quarry faced cut limestone exterior laid in a broken course with red ribbon pointing with ashlar finished limestone foundation; features a blend of Romanesque Revival and French Renaissance style elements; two corner towers topped by a plain, trimmed parapet; distance front entrance with detailed heavy quoin surrounds and stone dentils; asphalt shingle roof with 5 gable dormers & 1 shed dormer; all dormers are clapboard sided with multi light sash; large first storey plate glass windows with detailed cut stone surround; second storey window openings composed of 1 over 1 sash windows with splayed stone arches; limestone band extends around the west and north facades of the building underneath the second storey windows; one of the few early 20th century commercial structures remaining; played a significant role in the Village of Elgin; connection to the Imperial Bank of Commerce (CIBC)

properties.Name: Former Manse for Lundy's Lane United Church
properties.Statement: Very similar in style to the VIA Rail Station built in in 1879. Estimated c. 1872.

properties.Name: Gus' Pawn Shop/Thorburn's Drug Store
properties.Statement: This mid nineteenth century building owned by Theodore W. Woodruff was once a post office in 1913, with a lock up at the rear.  The false front façade was a late nineteenth century addition.  The building retains its metal shopfront cornice and bold cornice at the top of the facade.

properties.Name: Portage Road (Queenston-Chippawa Portage Road)
properties.Statement: Following the cession of the east bank of the Niagara River to the United States in 1783, the British authorities felt compelled to transfer the portage road around Niagara Falls to the west bank of the river. Opened in 1789 by a group of private traders led by Robert Hamilton, the road between Queenston and Chippawa, became the official government route in 1791. Until the completion of the Welland Canal in 1829 and the building of railways in the 1850's, it was the principal link in trade, travel and war between Lake Ontario and the upper lakes.
properties.Attributes: Historical Road

properties.Statement: The house (c.1840) follows the style of the regency cottage popular in the 1840's. It is recognized by its square plan with a low hip roof and symmetrical arrangement of openings across the front facade. The front door case retains its transom above the sidelights however the door is a replacement of an earlier 4 by 8 panel door. This was James Forsyth's second home in Drummondville. His first was located on the site of St. Mary's Ukrainian church. For many years Isaac Culp owned the house and farmed the surrounding land. Forsyth was one of the first ten families to settle in this area in 1783.
properties.Attributes: Overall height, scale, and massing; symmetrical façade and side elevations; one storey red brick framed rectangular floor plan in Regency Cottage style house; cut stone foundation; two-over-two sash window with a stone lintel and stone sill on either side of the central door; two two-over-two sash windows with stone lintels that are on each side elevations; three transom windows above the lintel and four vertical side windows on either side of the central door; the lintel has a row of plain moulding with a row of dentils underneath

properties.Name: Bradley Octagon House
properties.Statement: The house (c. 1906) is a very late version of the octagonal design proposed by Orson S. Fowler (1809-87) and used for homes mostly in the 1850's and 60's. Originally covered by clapboard, this house was later sided with insulbrick and presently is covered with vinyl siding. The house was most likely built by James Parker, a carpenter by trade, after he purchased the lot from George W. Ellis in April 1905. The house remained in his family until 1989 when his granddaughter Joyce Bradley sold it.

properties.Name: Laura Secord House
properties.Statement: The house (c. 1837) represents a modest Upper Canadian style cottage of the mid 19th century. Most of its decoration is concentrated on the entranceway, which features two flanking doric columns supporting an entablature, side- lights and a transom now enclosed by a modern porch. The roof and interior were rebuilt after a fire in 1930.  War of 1812 heroine Laura Secord (1775-1868) bought the house in 1841 and lived there the rest of her life, operating a private school to support herself. The house was first owned by James Cummings, a merchant and landowner who was the first reeve of Chippawa and whose father Thomas was the first settler in 1783.
properties.Attributes: One and a half storey structure with a symmetrical three bay façade; constructed of red brick laid in common bond and with a rubble stone foundation; irregular limestone quoins built into the building's corners; reconstructed medium-pitch gable roof is clad in asphalt shingles; clapboard siding on the gable ends; corbelled, stacked brick chimneys placed near each gable end of the roof; wooden arbour sheltering front entrance; solid wooden door with six recessed panels, flanked by two engaged Doric fluted columns, and featuring a simple entablature, transom and sidelights; two Venetian style windows with 12 over 8 sash and sidelights, plain trim sill, and a splayed brick arch; 4 over 4 windows with plain trim in the east (2) and west (1) gable ends; associated with Laura Secord, known for her contribution in the War of 1812-1814; associated with Thomas Cummings and James Cummings, prominent figures in the founding and development of Chippawa

properties.Name: Olsen-Sottile Insurance
properties.Statement: The Norwich beautification program of 1966 produced a few cosmetic changes to the building. The  red brick façade (c. 1895)  was painted dark grey, the windows were furnished with shutters painted bright yellow and the window trim was done in the same colour. Further the significance of this building lies not in its current appearance, which is unremarkable, but in its late Victorian origins (built by Andrew Hawkins for owners Andrew and Elizabeth Hawkins)  and the contribution it makes as one component of a late nineteenth/early twentieth century block which remains intact. It is a currently Olsen-Sottile insurance.

properties.Name: Oswald-Holburn House
properties.Statement: The west end of the present house (c.1835) was  originally a two-room office building with brick walls of double thickness. This entire section is now the living room, with the original cast iron fireplace in the north end. The front porch is a recent addition. To the rear is a small brick smokehouse. James Oswald, who lived in the house on the corner immediately to the west and is said to be the original owner, used the office when managing his brewery, which was located to north of the railroad line on Highway 8.

properties.Name: St. Patrick's Church
properties.Statement: The red sandstone masonry of the Church (c. 1895) was laid by George Seales and the carpentry done by Waugh and Robertson. The most prominent features of its Gothic styling are the high, octagonal spire and large rose window on the east gable end was built by Newman Brothers Co. The original slate tile roof was replaced in 1995. The Rectory to the south was built c 1897-99. The Church was built at a cost of $24,000 and the work was done under the direction of Reverend Dominic Thomas o' Malley.

properties.Name: Cummington Square
properties.Statement: Cummington Square is a public park dedicated for the use of all citizens.  The shape of Cummington Square is that of a rectangle having had a portion of the square taken in 1958 to create parking spaces along the east side. The square is delineated by streets on all four sides. The square is a level plot of ground covered with grass and crossed by concrete pathways.  The light poles and heads are modern; photographs of the original fixtures are available.  The bandstand occupies the location and footprint of the first bandstand erected in the 1920's.  The current structure is much altered from the original appearance, such that it is difficult to identify any significant architectural features.  It is the location, shape, size general form and long history as a place for music which are of importance.  The Cenotaph/War Memorial including the fence and flag pole are important elements physically and socially.  These elements were altered during an upgrading of the square in the late 1990's. They are maintained by the city in consultation with the Royal Canadian Legion-Chippawa Br. 396 as is a commemorative plaque located on the base of the bandstand.  A Parks Canada heritage plaque is located in the square which outlines the history of Chippawa. Cummington Square is part of the original Crown patent of 200 ac. granted in 1784 to Thomas Cummings. Thomas Cummings was a founding father of Chippawa and a leading citizen.  Both Thomas and his son James were prominent merchants contributing to the early economic development of Chippawa.  Cummings and his descendants dedicated the lands to the municipality as a village square and a site for a town hall.  A town hall was never built on this site.  The square is flanked on all four sides by streets.  Centrally located in the Chippawa business district it served as the hub of activity surrounded on three sides by commercial buildings. Many of these same 19th and 20th century buildings still face the square.  Cummington Square is a public park which has continuously served as the centre for community activities.  Citizens have gathered there to enjoy music played in the bandstand, attend a memorial event or to participate in one of the many public functions.  The square has been used to honour those who fought in WW 1, WW 2 and the Korean War.  The square holds significant cultural value because of its association with an early settler and business operator, its connection to early commercial life, its importance as a public place for civic activities and its presence as a park used to recognize the contributions of the community's residents.
properties.Attributes: The location and layout of the square being flanked on all four sides by streets; continuous use as public park; name of Cummings family that donated the land for the civic square; the band stand although not original allows the square to continue to be used for public gatherings whether it is for entertainment or memorial occasions; cenotaph and memorial plaques

properties.Name: Russell Cottage
properties.Statement: Built in separate phases in the early 19th century, the house (c. 1830) exhibits differing styles. The first phase (before 1830) had a stone foundation and floor joists/rafters of logs. In the second phase (1830-35), lumber was used to build the north side gable and the verandah with its notable diamond-patterned Stamford treillage. Early owners of the house were Rheddy Cusack and merchant/saddler Andrew Rorback, who may have built it. Its third owner, Matthew Ottley, is believed to have given the house much of its present appearance. It is named for Grace Russell, a later occupant and widow of the first Minister of the Stamford Presbyterian Church.
properties.Attributes: Built in the local Regency vernacular style, blending details from several styles of 19th century architecture; one storey dwelling with an asymmetrical four bay façade; mortared stone foundation; verandah extending across the entire west (front ) façade which has 6 posts and features trellis known as the "Stamford Trellis"; original 6 over 6 window sash window openings on the west (front), north and east (rear) facades; eave returns on gable ends; housed several prominent figures in the former Township of Stamford, including Grace Russell, widow to Stamford Presbyterian's first minister Rev. John Russell; connected to the history and development of the former Township of Stamford and the Stamford Presbyterian Church

properties.Name: Ferguson House
properties.Statement: The house (c. 1900) was originally owned by Mary Ferguson.  In 1926, it was sold to Albert W. Marsh who was the manager of Marsh Grape Juice Company who used it as a rental property.  It was built in the late Queen Anne Revival Style.  It was an asymmetrical form with a complex roof.  The bay window on the second floor extends to form a third floor tower.  The wrap around porch features columns and a pediment with intricate scroll work.  The broad stairway is well proportioned and flanked by stone pillars.  The tower has a bell shaped roof in six sections. There is a bay window at the front of the house at the ground level and there are two front doors.

properties.Name: Former Niagara Falls Museum--Aviary
properties.Statement: The original 1908 building consisted of a three and four storey concrete and brick building with steel frame and a flat roof for the Spirella Corset Factory.  It went through alterations in 1958 when the Niagara Falls Museum operated on the site (owned by the Sherman family).   In 2000, the building was sold and after alterations the Bird Kingdom opened in 2003.

properties.Name: Buchner House
properties.Statement: The exterior of the house (c. 1799) exhibits a blend of vernacular styles ranging from the mid 19th to the early 20th century. Initially a two-bay Italianate frame structure, its enclosed porch, extended roof slope and elongated dormer are alterations of the original form. The sash windows vary in size and pane configuration between the house and the front porch indicating separate periods of construction. The original lot, purchased by Christopher Buchner from father in law James Forsyth, was central to the Battle of Lundy's Lane on July 25, 1814. Buchner operated an early ferry service across the river. Donald Mackenzie, who lived here after 1851, built and operated the city's first observation tower of the battle site.
properties.Attributes: Proximity to the Lundy's Lane Battlefield; one and a half storey building clad in clapboard siding; medium pitch gable roof; a brick chimney on west side; enclosed veranda is a later addition; off centre front entrance; association with Buchner, Forsyth and Street families

properties.Name: Whirlpool House
properties.Statement: The building (c. 1796) is one of a very few surviving examples of lath and plaster construction of the late 18th and early 19th centuries. The ground floor, once a ballroom, has a barrel vault type ceiling with oak beams, and the east facade at one time had a long wooden verandah. It underwent major renovations in the 1940's. Built by Andrew Rorback (1774-1843), a loyalist from New Jersey, it was first a saddlery before becoming Rorback's Tavern. In its early days, it was a social venue and a popular place for political and business meetings. It was later purchased by James Oswald circa 1835 and became known as Whirlpool Inn.
properties.Attributes: One of the oldest homes in the area; one of the best known inns on the Portage Road and as Mr. Rorback was active in community affairs, his inn was a popular place to hold meetings and social events; the construction of lath and plaster is typical of the late Eighteenth and early Nineteenth Century; the style of this type of home represents is becoming increasingly hard to find

properties.Name: Alexander Robinson Residence
properties.Statement: The central part of the house  (c.1821) was built earlier with squared timber walls lined with brick. The north and south gable ends were added later and the structure covered in clapboard and given its Italianate styling. In 1969, the interior was entirely renovated the front porch was replaced and the exterior was covered in stucco. The house was owned by Susannah Alexander, widow of Hugh Alexander (1780-1817), the first merchant to open a store in Stamford. The original 2.5 acre lot later held a fruit farm, and the house offered accommodation  for tourists beginning in the 1920's. The house was owned by the Robinson family from 1913-1995.
properties.Attributes: One and a half storey, rectangular building with an asymmetrical five bay façade; exterior clad in white stucco, original clapboard siding still under the stucco; distinctive roof arrangement that incorporates three gables with projected eaves across the east (front) facade; central dormer, large gables; gabled portico supported by two Doric order columns, replaced the original hip-roofed verandah with paired pillar posts; 2 over 2 sash windows with segmental openings, wood surrounds and replacement louvered-style shutters; front door offset from centre, segmental in shape with wood surround; connected to prominent figure in the Stamford Township history, Hugh Alexander; landmark for the development of both the Stamford Green and historic Portage Road

properties.Name: Acres House/YWCA
properties.Statement: The building has elements of the Tudor Revival style of the first quarter of the 20th century, with its exposed wood beams. The central bay projects forward and is surmounted by a central  pediment in the roof. The front entrance is protected by a roof supported by brackets. The front entrance has a double door with sidelights. This was the home of H. R. Acres. He purchased the lot Aug. 22, 1923 from Mary Davy for $3,000 (American). H. G. Acres was the Chief Hydraulic Engineer for the Sir Adam Beck Generating Station no. 1. In 1942 the house was purchased by H.G. Acres & Company Ltd to become their offices. Later an addition was built on Barker Street. in 1955 the house was purchased by the YWCA to be used as a residence.

properties.Name: Doran-Marshall-Burke House
properties.Statement: This house (c. 1886) is a remarkable example of the Queen Anne Revival style. Built of fine cream-coloured brick, it has a round corner tower with a conical roof, gable windows of various shapes and a curved verandah with a moulded frieze supported by slender columns. To the rear of the house is the original detached coach house. William l. Doran and his brother owned the Dominion Suspender Co. and Niagara Necktie factories in town. The house served as an unofficial social club and was the scene of both formal balls and many a wild party.
properties.Attributes: Two storey Queen Anne Revival style; multi-gabled roof with a built-in cornice gutter with scalloped cedar shingles, dentil moulding, and acorn drops under the eves; rounded tower on the southwest corner; constructed of yellow brick laid in stretcher bond; limestone block foundation; cone-shaped roof on the corner tower with wooden brackets and rectangular and  scalloped cedar shingles; two outset chimneys on the south and west facades; two gable ends with vertical wood slat siding, each containing an ogee window opening with plain surrounds; sweeping curved verandah with modern steel roofing, dentils, and seven Doric order columns; a number of window styles, including coloured glass transom, diamond cross patterns, and multiple square panes; building's fenestration primarily consists of rectangular window openings with plain limestone sills and flat brick arches; four windows on the west (rear) facade, six on the north facade, and three on the east (front) facade; two-storey coach house incorporating many of the features of the main building, including a cedar shingle roof, yellow brick construction, and articulated facades; known for its association with Doran and Marshall families both of whom were influential in the community

properties.Name: Oswald Residence
properties.Statement: An excellent example of the Regency Style, this house (c. 1835) features large, multipaned ground floor windows and a broad verandah with wood trellis supports across the south and west facades. The decorative iron fence, set in a stone base along the south and west borders of the lot, was imported from England. James Oswald was a local businessman who owned a brewery with his brother near St. David's, co-founded the 1854 survey of Clifton with Samuel Zimmerman, and was proprietor of the Whirlpool Inn. Part of the original 1978 designation by-law was repealed in 1993 to allow partioning of the lot (see Byl-aw 93-121).
properties.Attributes: One and a half storey dwelling with a symmetrical five bay façade; stucco exterior with a rubble stone foundation; low pitched gable roof clad in asphalt shingles; two large inset chimneys; central door features the original six panel door flanked by 4 paned sidelights and pilasters; two sets of French doors on either side of central door with another two sets on the south elevation (six sets total); broad veranda along the west (front) and south facades of the house featuring a bell cast roof supported by a wooden trellis, known as 'Stamford Treillage'; treillage consists of 2 posts with diamond pattern lattice with interconnected elliptical wood arches springing from a wood corbel; two 6 over 6 sash on either gable end; stone wall with iron fence bordering the property on two sides, made of cast iron, in a scroll work pattern and is mortised to the stone caps with lead; owned by James Oswald, a prominent business man in the Niagara area, owner of one of the most profitable industries of his time, and business partner to Samuel Zimmerman, founder of the Town of Clifton; proximity to Portage Road and on the corner of two historic streets in the former Township of Stamford

properties.Name: Stamford Presbyterian
properties.Statement: The present Church (c. 1871) was built on the foundation of an earlier structure. Features of note are the balustrade on top and triple lancet windows on the front of the tower, and round stained glass window above the main door. The tower was originally three-sided with a back added later and each corner was once topped by a pinnacle. The original Presbyterian Meeting House, built in 1791 of logs, served the earliest settlers of the area, many of whom were of Scottish descent who chose lands atop the Escarpment. The churchyard to the south, called "God's half acre" when it opened in 1784 is the resting place of many of Stamford’s founding citizens.

properties.Name: Queen Victoria Park
properties.Statement: The Queen Victoria Park Cultural Heritage landscape is located within the City of Niagara Falls, within the Regional Municipality of Niagara, which is located south of Lake Ontario and north of Lake Erie, west of the United States border. Queen Victoria Park is situated approximately 4 kilometers east of the Queen Elizabeth Way (QEW) highway, which runs parallel to the Niagara River.  The Queen Victoria Park Cultural Heritage Landscape includes the parkland which was historically named Queen Victoria Park (QVP), extending from Oakes Garden Theatre and Clifton Hill to Dufferin Islands and is identified on the 1896 plan for the area. These lands are significant as they include to the Niagara Gorge, Niagara River, and Niagara Falls to the east, with the moraine to the west. Queen Victoria Park has evolved significantly since its conception, yet has remained true to its original function, being primarily related to tourism, sport/leisure, while incorporating power-generating facilities in an aesthetically pleasing designed picturesque landscape dotted with built features including (but not limited to) structures, circulation systems, monuments, and gardens.
properties.Attributes: Natural landforms and water features, circulation, vegetation and gardens, views, and built heritage structures

properties.Name: Karn-Brown-Gauld House
properties.Statement: The home (c. 1809) was massively constructed by Andrew Karn (1757-1829) with heavy oak and walnut beams, and walls of local limestone nearly three feet thick. The stone has since been covered with stucco and a wing has been added to the eastern wall. The front porch is recent and the interior of the house has been much renovated and modernized. The Battle of Beaverdams (June 24, 1813) took place nearby. Contractor and mason John Brown bought the property in 1870. It became Cloverhill Farm, where dairy cows were raised by the Brown family until 1972. The property is now a nursery run by the Gauld family.

properties.Name: Oak Hall
properties.Statement: Built (c. 1928) at a cost of $500,000, the mansion exhibits the Perpendicular or Tudor Gothic style. Its 130 foot facade features a  porte-cochere with Tudor arches at the entrance, projecting gables with raking parapets and leaded windows, some with ogee arches. Inside is the great hall and many other rooms decorated with carved wood panels. Magnate and philanthropist Harry Oakes built his hall around a portion of Clark Hill, a mansion dating from the 1850's. The Oakes family lived there until 1934. The hall was a R.C.A.F. convalescent hospital during the Second World War and was purchased by Niagara Parks in 1959.

properties.Name: St. John's United Church
properties.Statement: This structure (c. 1861) replacing an earlier log church built in 1834, was built under the supervision of George Burger. Corbelled brickwork decorates the upper facade and walls. The front tower and steeple were added in the 1890's, and the base of the steeple once held a four-faced clock.  St. John's is the oldest congregation in Willoughby. The Church was once used by three groups: the Lutherans, Evangelical Reformed and the Pennsylvania Dutch. The services were originally in German, with ministers from Buffalo officiating. The cemetery on the opposite side of Sodom Road was purchased by the Church in 1845.

properties.Name: Alanson Ross Carriage Works
properties.Statement: The original building on this property was the home of Alanson Ross and later became the Alanson Ross Carriage works.  The original home was built around 1830 and displays characteristics of the Neoclassical style with its low pitched gable roof and pair of end chimneys.  It also has elements of Classical Revival style with its projecting central portion and its roof pediment that hints of a temple like facade.  It has undergone many revisions over the years. Most recently it has been used as the Patterson Funeral Home.

properties.Name: Post Office- Customs House
properties.Statement: This structure (c. 1885) is an impressive example of late 19th century Public Architecture. It exhibits the detailed, cut and finished limestone construction of that period, with  massive round-headed archways, quoins, heavy stringcourses and diamond patterning on the gables. Originally known as the Dominion Public Building, it was designed by government architect Thomas Fuller (who designed the first Parliament buildings in Ottawa), and was constructed at a cost of $30,000. It served as post office (1885-1930), customs house (1885-1952) and the local police station (1952-1976). Address was changed in January 2003 - formerly known as 4582 Zimmerman.
properties.Attributes: Romanesque Revival style; exterior made of quarry faced limestone blocks laid in a random course; finished limestone is used for the building's decorative elements; separate similar smaller structure on the west elevation; truncated hip roof originally clad with slate shingles; cross gables with heavy stringcourse bands, diamond patterned tympanums, and central floral ornaments; dormers placed along the roof; finials placed on the gable and dormers; block modillions beneath the eaves; asymmetrical three bay facade; main entry on the west facade contains a large round headed arch and a wood six panel door; southwest corner features two magnificent round-headed arches supported by limestone pillars with Corinthian details; central segmental window opening that has a splayed limestone arch on the west and south facades; connection to the development and core areas of the Town of Clifton; connection to renowned government architect Thomas Fuller; significant location both for its ties to communication and government operations, and due to its service to the City and the community

properties.Name: Spence Weaver House
properties.Statement: The larger front section of the house (c. 1835) was constructed by Drummondville mason Henry Spence, while the rear wood frame wing was originally a settler's cabin dating to around 1800. An old brick scullery is also attached to the west side of the cabin and has remnants of an original cauldron and bread oven. A board and batten garage was added to the rear by the current owners. Stamford Township Lot 161 was first obtained from the crown by Haggai Skinner, who likely built the earlier cabin. It was later Henry Spence's farm from 1854 to 1885. In 1893, the house and property were purchased by David Weaver, and remained in the Weaver family until 1973. Mr. Spence came from England in 1834 and was noted for his fine brickwork.
properties.Attributes: Form and setting of the house on the remaining portion of the original homestead; simple but solid, 2 storey red brick dwelling with simple low pitched gable style roof and shallow eaves; 3 bays placed asymmetrically across front façade with 2 additional bays on wing addition on the west side; 6/6 windows; front door with double light transom above the door and sidelights that extend to top of the opening with rowlock arch; bricks scullery on west side of 2 storey portion; lack of decorative features; rubble stone foundation with ashlar cut limestone sills; recently re-established verandah along north facade of 2 storey portion

properties.Name: Niagara Falls Post Office
properties.Statement: The original structure (c. 1930) was 84 feet square and has since been enlarged to its present dimensions. Its art deco façade was designed by Findlay and Foulis and was constructed by Piggott Construction Co.  It has a simplified cornice and windows separated vertically by squared pilasters with ionic capitals and broken horizontally by stone panels. The interior was done with terrazzo floors marble and mahogany trim. Constructed at a cost of $100,000, the building was officially opened in January 1931. The addition stands on the site of the former manse of  St. Andrew's United Church which was demolished in 1961.

properties.Name: McNally Building
properties.Statement: Built between 1916 and 1920 by Ervin C. McNally--McNally's Drug Store operated at the site for many years. In later years the property was occupied by Coles Jewelry Store and My Country Delicatessen.
c. 1805, original owner noted as the Collard Family.

properties.Name: Bampfield Hall
properties.Statement: The house (c. 1875) is built primarily in the Gothic Revival style with pointed windows, a jerkinhead roof and gingerbread trim in the gable ends. Its upper structure exhibits the Second Empire style elements of a mansard roof on the central tower and iron cresting of the roof. The Classical style verandah was a later early 20th century addition. James Bampfield built this second home for his wife Margaret, who apparently never liked their first house.  For generations it remained the property of the Bampfields, as they rose to become one of the most prominent commercial families in Niagara Falls. The house was finally sold by the family in 1969.
properties.Attributes: Two storey dwelling with a rubble stone foundation, comprised of bricks laid in stretcher bond; brick painted in 2009 in a method known as "re-painting" to match the original red brick; asymmetrical three bay façade; three storey square tower with a high-pitched mansard roof; tower features bracketing beneath the eaves; iron cresting along the ridge; four gabled dormers in the tower containing bull's eye openings; dormers had original scalloped slate shingles; roof originally clad in slate shingles and is built in the jerkin head style; gables have gingerbread trim, associated with Gothic Revival details; paired lancet windows found beneath each of the gables; front elevation has a closed gable pediment and fish scale siding; veranda supported by 9 columns; pediment supported by 4 columns and features a series of dentils, heavy crown moulding and a fish scale pattern tympanum; front entrance has a cut and etched glass panel in the upper section of the door, a pair of 1 over 1 windows on the left and single window on the right; projecting bay featuring two segmental window openings, a bracketed entablature and wooden pilasters; two wings at rear of the main house; connected to the Bamfield family, who contributed to the social and economic development of the City

properties.Name: Loretto Academy (central parcel)
properties.Statement: The Academy (c. 1861)  is a massive structure made of stone. It is basically symmetrical in form. The north wing was completed in 1870 ten years before the main building. The north wing still has its simplified mansard roof and dormers, heavy roof cornice and large brackets arranged in pairs. The entrance to the north wing has a portico with supporting columns. In 1938 fire destroyed the interior and roof of the main building and its mansard roof and rotunda were not replaced. The central section has a wide long verandah. All walls of the building have prominent stone quoins. The basement level is defined by a jutting stone course and grey stone. Loretto Academy opened as a girls boarding school in 1861. It was located initially in Canada House a wayfarers tavern in front of the present Loretto Academy. It was repaired and remodeled  for the Five Sisters of Loretto who formed the first community. The inspiration for the establishment for a convent dates back to 1822.

properties.Name: McGlashan/Thomas House
properties.Statement: The McGlashan/Thomas house  (c. 1854) was constructed in two parts, most evident in the roof form. The earliest part, closest to Main Street, was two stories and square in plan. The two storey house is now rectangular in plan, measuring about 35 feet (11 metres) across its north facade and 45 feet (13.5 metres) from front to back.  It is of wood frame construction with a red brick veneer which has been more recently covered with stucco. The facade is arranged around 3 irregularly spaced bays. The style of the house is derived from principles of balance and proportion associated with Neo-Classical traditions.  The front of the house is now considered to be the elevation facing Bridgewater St. although the original front entrance appears to be on the west side of the southerly portion of the house. The McGlashan/Thomas house is in many ways central to the history of Chippawa, having been the residence of several individuals responsible for the economic growth of the town and of the Niagara area. Built during Chippawa's golden age as a port and manufacturing centre in the 1850's it was briefly the home of James McGlashan, a local merchant and later longtime treasurer of Welland County.  John Thomas and his family were involved in the establishment of local industry, co-founder of a major distillery and a grist mill.  In the 20th century, C. Ellison Kaumeyer as Director of Niagara Parks & Bridge Commission would work towards the restoration of Niagara's past as well as the development of its transportation network.  Although most of its original architecture has been modified over the years, the house remains part of a heritage neighbourhood in which the historical homes of past civic leaders, artists, authors, and professionals have been constructed over the past 150 years.

properties.Name: Earl Thomas House
properties.Statement: Earl Thomas House exhibits many Tudor style characteristics: steeply pitched roof, multiple prominent gables, half timbering, a large dominant chimney, small multi-pane sash. 6320 Pine Grove is significant for its association with original owner, Earl A. Thomas,  prominent person in the wine industry both locally and nationally. Born in 1894 in Stamford and began working at T.G.Bright's Wines in 1916. He rose to become President of the Company and remained so until his retirement in 1959. The Thomas's owned the property for 37 years, followed by Charles and Ruth Dunnett for the next 27 years. The architects, Findlay and Foulis built many significant buildings in the City: Table Rock House, Niagara Parks Buildings - Refractory Restaurant, Administration building; General Brock Hotel and Oak Hall.
properties.Attributes: Large property consisting of four lots creates a significant setting; the Tudor Revival House exhibits a full range of architectural detail associated with the style; steeply pitched roof with prominent gables; original window openings with brick sills laid with headers facing outward, flat arch with soldier course; round headed front door made of vertical plants with black metal hardware enclosed in a projecting brick vestibule with bellcast roof and corbelled brick at the eaves; red brick on first storey; dark half timber and light stucco exterior cladding on second storey; large dominant chimney in a central location on the front of the house; exterior of sunroom is red brick laid in a herringbone pattern; several significant mature specimen trees planted on property

properties.Name: Abigail Frolick House
properties.Statement: c. 1865 with original owner noted as Frolick.

properties.Name: Barry Block
properties.Statement: The Barry Block was the site of the Woolworth Store during the 1940s.

properties.Name: First Church of Christ Scientist
properties.Statement: In the 1920s, a Christian Science Society was formed in the Niagara Area.  A Reading Room and Lending Library was established in the Church edifice on Jepson Street, when the Church was opened in 1935.

properties.Name: Stone Building at the Halfway
properties.Statement: The 'halfway' was the halfway point used during the operation of the horse drawn railway between the Queenston Dock area to Chippawa.  This is the point where the team of horses would be changed.  The stone building on the property is approximately 300 feet square and has a low pitched gable roof.  There are two windows on the sides of the building which itself is set slightly into the ground.
properties.Attributes: Single storey stone building set slightly into the ground; stone laid in random rubble coursing; low pitched gable roof; window on each side; doorway opening on north side; limestone lintels; prominent setting corner of Portage Rd and Stanley Ave; association with use of property as halfway point for exchange of horses used in the Erie & Ontario Railroad

properties.Name: Our Lady of Peace Church
properties.Statement: The original north wing and central section of the building were built in 1894 by Piggott Construction Co.; the south wing in 1926.  The north wing was damaged by fire in November 1967 and later demolished.  Constructed of cut limestone, it features massive round-arched arcades supported by pillars, heavy window arches/surrounds and round corner towers with conical roofs on the surviving south wing. The Carmelites came to Niagara Falls at the invitation of Toronto Archbishop John Lynch who donated the property near the Falls.  Originally a hospice, the building housed Mount Carmel College from 1919 to 1979, which it became the Mount Carmel Spiritual Centre.

properties.Name: Former Lyon's Creek United Church
properties.Statement: The former Lyon’s Creek Church, a Wesleyan Methodist Church, (c. 1861) was built in a vernacular Italianate style with a balanced facade and segmental arches. Carpentry in the church was done by Alex Hurst and the brickwork by John Sennet. Iron reinforcement bars have been installed on the upper walls at the level of the window arches some of which exhibit stress cracking.  The local Methodist circuit was founded by George Neal in 1796, and the original Church built on this site in 1806 was the first in Crowland. The brick for the present Church was made by Reuben Buckner in his kiln at  white pigeon (where Lyon's Creek enters Willoughby) the huge oak in the churchyard is over 250 years old.
properties.Attributes: One storey with a symmetrical three bay façade; rectangular in shape measuring 9.14 m x 12.8 m; medium pitch metal gabled roof, with plain soffit and fascia; composed of red brick laid in stretcher bond with a rubble stone foundation; above the first storey is a raised brick stringcourse band that runs the course of the north (front) facade; iron reinforcement bars above the window arches to assist in stabilizing the walls; front entrance features a simple rectangular wooden door with a segmental 5-light transom, a rowlock arch and a plain limestone threshold; segmental window openings, with multi-pane, coloured glass, rowlock arch and limestone sill; two windows on the north (front) facade, three on the west facade, and two on the east facade, where the addition is located; connected to the development of the Methodist church in the Niagara area; site used as a barracks during the War of 1812-1814, and was involved in the Battle of Cook's Mill

properties.Name: Berengaria Farm
properties.Statement: Built in a massive, unadorned Greek Revival style, the house (c. 1846) features triple brick walls (the original red bricks are now covered with yellow ones), heavy stone lintels and sills. Part of the rear wing is a limestone rubble shed which was constructed c.1803 presently the front facade has a wood portico attached.  Lot 102 was originally granted in 1803 to Benajah Williams, who built the stone shed. The house was built by John Campbell Garden, a native of New Brunswick who had, as a lieutenant in the royal newfoundland regiment, fought with General Brock at Detroit and had been captured by US troops.

properties.Name: Navy Island
properties.Statement: The British used Navy Island from 1761 to 1764 as a shipyard in which to build the first British decked vessels to sail the upper lakes. These were essential in maintaining the supply lines westward during Pontiac's uprising, 1763-4. Thereafter the island remained undisturbed until 14 December 1837 when William Lyon Mackenzie, after being defeated at Toronto, led a "Patriot" army from Buffalo to occupy it. Swift reaction by local militia and British regulars prevented his moving to the mainland and on 14 January 1838, facing a hopeless situation, he abandoned the island.  Navy Island National Historic Site of Canada is a heavily wooded, uninhabited island on the Canadian side of the Niagara River just above Niagara Falls, Ontario. In the 1760s, Navy Island became the first British shipyard to serve the Upper Great Lakes and, during the Rebellions of 1837, was the seat of William Lyon Mackenzie’s exiled government. The island features many surviving archaeological resources. Official recognition refers to the entire island.
properties.Attributes: Entire Island

properties.Name: Loretto Academy (south parcel)
properties.Statement: Associated with the Loretto Academy.  The East Lawn and iron gate along the property line are its historical features.

properties.Name: Toronto Power Generating Station Complex
properties.Statement: The structure (c. 1906), designed by E.J. Lennox and built by Bevely R. Value,  was built in a Classical Renaissance style with north and south wings attached to a central section. Details include horizontal channeling, roundel windows, ionic columns and an ornate balustrade atop the entablature. The north end has a semicircular bay with scroll buttresses crowned by pyramidal finials. The first Canadian-owned generating plant on the river, it was the creation of Toronto entrepreneurs William Mackenzie, Henry Pellatt and Frederick Nicholls. built on land reclaimed from the river, the plant generated up to 125,000 horsepower of electricity with the generators connected by driveshafts to the turbines 150 feet below.

properties.Name: Glenview Mansion
properties.Statement: This large home (c. 1870) consists of a square-plan main building with two rear wings. Built in the Italianate style it has a projecting central bay capped by a closed pediment and bay windows flanking the front entrance. Originally, the roof had a belvedere surrounded by a wrought iron railing; it has been replaced by dormers.  Brick was used to produce such decorative elements as quoins, window labels and the four large chimneys. Much of the brick has been covered with stucco. The original Victorian porch has been removed from the entrance. The house was built by John Drew on his 75 acre farm which he purchased in 1869. In 1881, he sold the house to Dr. John Ferguson, who was twice elected  Member of Parliament in 1882 and 1887. R. P. Slater, who served as Mayor of Niagara Falls in 1899-1901,1906-07, and 1909, purchased the house and lands in 1893. The original address was 4223 Terrace Avenue.
properties.Attributes: Italianate vernacular architecture from the mid-Victorian period; large two storey detached dwelling; rectangular form, with a square main section and two rectangular tails; current stucco exterior and rubble stone foundation; brick was used for many of the decorative elements of the house; three chimneys near the northeast, southeast, and southwest corners; low pitch hip roof, typical of the Italianate architectural style; broad eaves with tongue and groove soffit supported by paired brackets; small wooden gable with raking cornices; closed pediment with recessed tympanum and brackets; shed dormers; modern metal double doors, with glass panels and segmental transom; 2 projecting bays containing 2 over 2 sash windows with hood moulds; the porch on north side has sloped roof, four posts with curved scroll brackets; connected to several prominent figures in the history of the City of Niagara Falls including John Drew, John Ferguson, and R.P. Slater; relevant to the social and political history of the City of Niagara Falls; positioned high on large property at the end of a long driveway overlooking the Niagara River

properties.Name: Queenston-Chippawa Hydro-Electric Development
properties.Statement: This generating station, built between 1917 and 1922, was considered the world’s first true hydroelectric megaproject. Its massive scale required the use of construction equipment, power conversion units, and a power canal of an unprecedented magnitude. The Hydro-Electric Power Commission of Ontario was responsible for this feat of engineering. Under the chairmanship of Sir Adam Beck, it expanded the plant’s capacity to supply inexpensive power to towns and cities, fueling the growth of industry, while supporting rural electrification. The Queenston-Chippawa Development was renamed the Sir Adam Beck Generating Station in 1950.

properties.Name: Red Oak Tree (on lot line between 6187 Clare Cres and 6149 Cuviello Court)
properties.Statement: 250-300 year old red oak tree
properties.Attributes: 250-300 year old red oak tree

properties.Name: Marsena Biggar House
properties.Statement: The small arched window in the gable and the ornate brackets around the veranda hint at the building's Victorian origins. This property is  of special interest as it still retains its original carriage house at the rear of the building. The carriage house  (c. 1871) is of board and batten construction. The house is presently covered with asbestos siding. This was the family home of the Marsena Biggar family. Marsena purchased an irregular shaped lot of just over 2 acres in 1871. The lot went as far west as Main Street and as far south as the late John Misener's land. It surrounded the Kick's property, located on Main Street on three sides. Marsena was a teacher in the public school system from 1851-1853 at Ferry (Clifton) Road School.

properties.Name: Carnegie Library
properties.Statement: The building (c. 1910) was designed by William Nichols and built by Alonzo Robertson. It features a raised limestone block basement and yellow brick quoins. Its Neoclassical details include the front portico with brick columns and an egg and dart motif, and a central gable with a closed pediment, an entablature with flat modillions and a semicircular fanlight. The Niagara Falls Carnegie library was one of 111 libraries built between 1901 and 1923 in Ontario as the result of the philanthropy of Andrew Carnegie. The cost of construction was approximately $15,000. It served the community for 64 years until the new Victoria library was opened in 1974.
properties.Attributes: Polychromatic exterior of red brick laid in stretcher bond and yellow brick; raised limestone foundation with quarry face finish, and red ribbon mortar; symmetrical five bay façade with the central three bays projecting forward; truncated hip roof, including a central gable with a closed pediment; centred portico and square, yellow-brick columns and pilasters; egg-and-dart decorative band above portico columns; detailed entablature with wooden dentils and wooden block modillions; large 2-pane and Venetian-styled windows; splayed, yellow brick arch with raised keystone above 1st and 2nd floor windows, a rowlock arch can be found on the basement windows; lead glass transom found above front entrance; built in cornice gutter

properties.Name: Queen Victoria Park

properties.Name: Skinner Block
properties.Statement: P.A. Skinner built the three storey red brick façade building (c 1893). Over the years it housed shoe shops, a fancy good store, a millinery shop, clothing shops, service shop, meat shop, bakery, electric shop, and an optometrist.

properties.Name: Thompson's Point
properties.Statement:
Thompson’s Point is located on the North side of the Niagara River above the Niagara Whirlpool, approximately 5.5kms to the Northwest of Niagara Falls and approximately 19kms south of Lake Ontario. It is formally bounded by the Niagara River Parkway to the North, and by the Niagara River (and gorge edge) to the south. The area is defined by natural and built landscape features: the gorge wall on each side; the Niagara River and Whirlpool below; the landing platform of the Whirlpool Aero Car; the parkway access and viewpoint at the upper level edge. Thompson’s Point, associated with early settlement in the area and the Thompson family (1782) from which the property takes its name, is a significant property of cultural heritage value and prominent site in the development of eco-tourism since the mid-19th century in Niagara Falls. The Thompson family quarried limestone on the riverside edge of the property and processed it on site, producing agricultural lime, and during the War of 1812, the quarry was considered important to the war effort.
John Thompson also built a stairway for the public to get down to the Whirlpool (1848). The location along the crest of the Niagara gorge provides a key access point to observe the Whirlpool, with the Niagara Parkway scenic lookout stop at Thompson point providing panoramic views and important view sheds across the Niagara River Gorge and Whirlpool below. The site provides a connecting point for the Whirlpool Aero Car, its design and construction in 1916 is an example of early tourism and economic development in the Niagara area, and was recognized internationally for its feats of engineering. The site shares connection to the development of the generating stations and hydroelectric power in Niagara as a depository for the excavated material. The property is adjacent to the Niagara River and therefore has archaeological potential for Pre-Contact aboriginal artifacts and a spiritual significance. The Niagara River Gorge (and by association Thompson’s Point) has a strong relationship with the entire province and country through its stunning landscape that evokes emotion in the generations of people that see and share it. The Thompson property remains a significant part of cultural tourism within Niagara Falls today.  The site also has strong relationships to historical evolution of the area, the arrival of Loyalists, support of the War of 1812, Ontario Power, local transportation and railway development, and engineering advancements.
properties.Attributes: Location, Views and Vistas, Aero car and landing site

properties.Name: Lemon Homestead
properties.Statement: This house (c. 1800) survives as an example of an early 19th century settler's dwelling. It was constructed of stucco over frame with a full l-shaped basement and French doors opening onto a verandah extending across an east wing. Gothic Revival elements--a central gable and window and roof brackets were likely added during renovations after 1850. The west side sun room was added in 1935. Lawrence Lemon (1771-1842), a Loyalist originally from Pennsylvania, was granted lot 71 in 1798. During the War of 1812, the house served as an army barracks.

properties.Name: Christian Reform Church
properties.Statement: The Church was built in 1916 at a cost of $16 000.  It originally was the First Baptist Church of Niagara Falls.  As the congregation grew, the decision was to build a new church and the Christian Reformed Church purchased the property for $40 000.  They have been worshipping in the building for over 100 years.

properties.Name: (former) St. Stephens Anglican Church
properties.Statement: St. Stephens Church was designed by C.H. Acton Bond of Toronto.  Robertson Construction Company in Niagara Falls built the church.  In 1922 St. Stephen's opened on the property as a missionary church.  In 1951 it became a parish with Rev. C. Gray Eakins as the rector. The church is of solid brick construction with a chancel that was finished in fir and had a maple floor.

properties.Name: McClive/Rosbergs
properties.Statement: The Block was constructed by Jacob Lovell between 1904-05 for Frederick W. McClive.  He was a billard room proprietor and paid $4800 for the lot.  The first floor had the Fielding and Co. clothing and shoe store and J.J. Kerr Dry Good.  On the second floor were insurance company offices, a customs broker, a dentist, and other businesses.  The third floor had four large flats.  In the basement was George Sidey's barber shop and McClive's Billard Parlour and Bowling Alley.  There were later stores on the site including:  F.W. Woolworth and Col, Metropolitan Stores, Dominion Stores, and later was part of Rosberg's.
