properties.Name: Munford House
properties.Statement: This house (c. 2879) was built in a straightforward Italianate style popular in residences of the 1870's and 1880's. Much of its original wood detailing is still in place, including the  vergeboards in the gable ends and refined porches with decorative scrollwork. The projecting bay window on the east side referred to as a summer porch was added on in 1898. Thomas Munford (1840-1910), the original owner, was a successful local mason and contractor who had worked on the Canada Southern Railroad and on contracts as far away as Virginia. From 1916 to 1956, the house was owned by the Niagara Falls Y.W.C.A.

properties.Name: Church Residence
properties.Statement: The house (c. 1810) maintains much of its original Loyalist styling with its balanced facade and gabled roof. The central gable, front porch, bay window and window trim are Italianate elements likely added in the 1860's or 70's. The rear and interior have been extensively renovated. The original owner was Andrew Rorback, who purchased the property in 1809 and opened a tavern in what is now the Whirlpool House across Portage Road. His widow Matilda sold the house in 1857 to Munson Church who made the exterior renovations. Church's lane was named for him.
properties.Attributes: Loyalist style, two storey dwelling with asymmetrical tree bay façade; medium pitch gable roof; balanced front façade; stucco exterior situated on a stone foundation; balustraded porch on front (west) elevation; later additions include projected bay window on front facade, balcony and large outset chimney on rear facade; small pediment above each window; louvered shutters

properties.Statement: Land was originally given to Thomas Cummings by the Crown in 1794.  Owners include Oliver T. Macklem.

properties.Name: Buckley McMurray House
properties.Statement: The home was built for William McMurray's bride, Grace Menzie, in 1893.  Descendents lived in the house until 1985.  The home has several elements associated with the Queen Anne style such as the asymmetrical façade with a central tower, the overall large mass, 2 storeys, a steeply pitched roof, tall chimney and verandah.  Many of the windows are double hung and paired on the first and second floors. Within the interior there are several unusual items--decorative gingerbread fretwork supports the staircase to the second storey, and there is detailed woodwork on the staircase, moulding, baseboards, mantels, etc.  There are two large ionic columns that separate the living room from the dining room.  Other features are the embossed doorknobs and hinges and parquet flooring in the living and dining rooms.
properties.Attributes: Interior: decorative wood spindle work under the staircase in main entrance; 2 ionic order columns in between the living room and dining room. Exterior: two storey asymmetrical structure; steep roof and large chimney; large verandah with fish scale shingles; large prominent central tower; eave brackets; prominent location on rise above River Road; large red oak tree on front lawn estimated to be 225-250 years old; association with William McMurray, former City Treasurer

properties.Name: Nathaniel Dett Chapel-BME Church
properties.Statement: The building (c. 1836) was moved to its present site in 1856 using logs as rollers. A rear addition was built at the turn of the century as the Minister's residence; it is now the Norval Johnson library. The church was originally covered with clapboard. The land for the church was donated  by Oliver Parnell and his wife Matilda, both of whom had escaped from slavery in the U.S. For many people who followed the underground railroad and settled in Niagara Falls, this Church served as their spiritual, social and educational centre of their community.
properties.Attributes: One storey structure with a symmetrical three bay façade; simple form and medium-pitch gable roof associated with the Loyalist style; original clapboard exterior restored in 2003; foundation is made of a quarry faced stone; enclosed porch at the centre of the north (front) facade, featuring gavel roof, 6-panelled double doors, and two 1 over 1 sash windows; roundel containing coloured glass quatrefoil; addition at the rear of the building with a medium pitch gable roof and three double hung sash windows; lancet windows with multi-paned coloured glass; connection to man of Niagara's most recognized Black citizens including Nathaniel Dett, Oliver and Mathilda Pernell, and Burr Plato

properties.Statement: c. 1840.  Original owner noted as Hamilton Ker.

properties.Name: Jacob Hixon House
properties.Statement: c. 1846, original owner noted as Jacob Hixon.

The home (c. 1903) was built by Peter and Rebecca Heximer. Peter paid $200 for the lot that was part of the Alanson Ross Estate.  Peter worked as a laborer for Cyanamid of Canada.  The house draws inspiration from the Queen Anne Revival style.  It is an example of an early 20th century working class family home.

properties.Name: John Misener Jr House
properties.Statement: John Misener Jr. purchased 3/4 acre on Peer Street from his father Captain John Misener in 1855 for 75 pounds. The house would have been constructed soon after. The house features an "Ontario Gothic" style central gable in the roof. The gable window design with a pediment is an adaptation of Italianate form. The field stone wall of the verandah would have been a later addition. The upper portion of the verandah features elaborate woodwork with turned posts. The chimneys are no longer present. John Misener Jr. was born in 1829. He would have been 26 when he purchased the land on Peer Street from his father. Fis father Captain John Misener owned and operated a wagon making business on the corner of Main Street and Peer Street. John Misener Jr. assumed the wagon making business after his father’s death in 1855.

properties.Name: Copper Beech Tree
properties.Statement: Copper Beech Tree at Drummond Hill Cemetery has become a local and regional cultural icon due to its historical association with the War of 1912 and in particular the Battle of Lundy's Lane.  Its colour symbolizes the blood that was shed while its dominant size and shape demonstrates the overall importance of the battle. It was planted in 1914 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the Battle of Lundy's Lane.
properties.Attributes: The strong cultural associations the City has for the tree including the memorializing of the War of 1812, more particularly, the Battle of Lundy's Lane in 1814; the orientation to Drummond Hill, enhancing the tree's visibility and marking the location of a significant battle; bark with elephant hind appearance; tree's rounded form with branches close to the ground; deciduous aspect of the tree resulting in leaves unfurling in the spring as soft green, gradually changing to a rich russet colour in the summer and ultimately to a tawny bronze colour in the fall.

properties.Name: Formerly the manse of Stamford Presbyterian Church
properties.Statement: built before 1825

properties.Name: Canadian Niagara Power Generating Station Complex (Niagara Parks Power Station)
properties.Statement: The Canadian Niagara Power Generating Station (CNP), also known as the William Birch Rankine Hydroelectric Power Station, is located in the City of Niagara Falls, within the Regional Municipality of Niagara. The generating station includes the powerhouse, outer forebay, the Niagara River Parkway bridge, the ice bridge, tailrace tunnel, ice-race channel, and regulating weir. Situated in Queen Victoria Niagara Falls Park, the CNP is considered to be part of the larger Queen Victoria Niagara Falls Park cultural heritage landscape. The CNP generating station was constructed between 1901 and 1927 and was decommissioned in 2006. The generating station is located on the western side of the Niagara River above Horseshoe Falls, on the former location of Cedar Island. It is one of three early 20th century power stations on the Canadian side of Niagara Falls. Ownership of the CNP was transferred to the Niagara Parks Commission (NPC) in 2009.
properties.Attributes: Exterior of the building and some interior components

properties.Name: Korean Presbyterian Church
properties.Statement: In 1920, the building of the Kitchener Street Union Church was undertaken following the union of multiple churches.  The church was designed by William Nichols, a local Niagara Falls architect.

properties.Name: Le Page House
properties.Statement: This house (c.1904) represents a more humble or middle class version of the Queen Anne Revival style, originally covered in clapboard and later with stucco. The square front tower is topped with a peaked roof and round pommel-like copper finial. Every other floor joist is a half log and the foundation walls appear to be earth and rubble. This subdivision, known as Wesley Park, was developed in 1885 by the Niagara Falls Camp Meeting Association as a Methodist resort. When the camp meeting venture failed, the lots were later sold off by lottery in 1887. Edith and Anson Book are listed as the original owners and James A. Anger is recorded as the builder.
properties.Attributes: Small scale Queen Anne style house; central tower with copper ball atop a finial; diamond pane casement windows in tower; steeply pitched roof; 12 panel front door with single light; front verandah supported by three Doric columns; property associated with Methodist Camp Meeting Association grounds

properties.Name: Old Bank of Hamilton/CIBC
properties.Statement: This five-sided block (c. 1894) exemplifies the transitional commercial architecture of the 1890's. Its original owner was Joseph and Mary Ganter, its architect was William Nichols, and it was built by W.H. Crowie & Sons. Its facade blends Victorian Italianate styling with more modern forms such as pronounced structural bays and large window openings. The ground floor was renovated in the 1920's during expansion of the banking offices and again in the late 1980's. It was the first large commercial block to be erected on the busy Queen Street-Erie Avenue axis. Its ground floor housed branches of the Bank of Hamilton (1902-24), Bank of Commerce (1924-61) and the CIBC (1961-85). The second floor held the office of the Niagara Falls City Solicitor from 1914-1968.

properties.Name: Mount Carmel
properties.Statement: The original north wing and central section of the building were built in 1894 by Piggott Construction Co. for the Carmelite Fathers; the south wing in 1926. The north wing was damaged by fire in November 1967 and later demolished. Constructed of cut limestone, it features massive round-arched arcades supported by pillars heavy window arches/surrounds and round corner towers with conical roofs on the surviving south wing. The Carmelites came to Niagara Falls at the invitation of Toronto Archbishop John Lynch, who donated the property near the Falls. Originally a hospice, the building housed Mount Carmel College from 1919 to 1979, when it became the Mount Carmel Spiritual Centre.

properties.Name: Old St. John's Anglican Church- Stamford Columbarium
properties.Statement: An example of early 19th century Canadian vernacular architecture, it was restored in 1985. Constructed of limestone covered with stucco, it features regency gothic windows, a sided bell tower, six-panel double wooden doors, buttresses along its southeast angle and an apsidal rear chancel. One of the oldest surviving Churches in Ontario, (c. 1825)  it was built on land donated by Captain R.H. Dee under the patronage of Lt. Gov. Sir Peregrine Maitland. It served as an important place of meeting on the well-travelled Portage Road between Queenston and Chippawa.
properties.Attributes: Symmetrical one-storey building with a balanced three-bay façade; made of local limestone, with an exterior stucco finish; cedar shake gable roof with a simple entablature and eave returns; 3 tall pointed arch window openings located on each side of building with plain sills and simple moulded trim, containing an 18 over 24 sash window with interlacing glazing bards; short, square tower that is placed in the centre of the west (front) facade and finished with clapboard siding; tower includes a plain entablature, four pinnacles, and a short bell cast metal spire, four pointed arch openings, containing a pair of lancet louvred openings, a small quatrefoil and four colonettes; 9-light window with interlacing glazing bars located above front entrance; two 16 over 16 sash on either side of front entrance; six paneled double door with a plain trim used for the main entrance; square datestone located above the entryway; one of the earliest Anglican churches in the province of Ontario; connection to several prominent figures in the area including:  Sir Peregrine Maitland, Lieutenant-Governor from 1818-1828, Reverend William Leeming, and Captain R.H. Dee, Esq; connection to the history of the Stamford Township, the designated Stamford Green, and the historic Portage Road

properties.Name: Holy Trinity Church
properties.Statement: The church (c. 1841), designed by John G. Howard,  is a fine example of the early English form of the Gothic Revival style. Its identifying features are the tall wooden crenellated parapet in front of the gable end, small pinnacles on the spire and a large almond-shaped or 'aureole' window in the central tower. From 1984-1991 it underwent a series of renovations. The present structure stands on the foundation of the 1821 church, burned by Rebel sympathizers in 1839. It served as one of the oldest and most prominent parishes in Upper Canada. Such notables as Edward VII, Laura Secord and Swedish opera singer Jenny Lind worshipped there.
properties.Attributes: Gothic Revival style, with lancet windows and tall steeple; one storey building with a symmetrical three bay façade; brick laid in Flemish bond with limestone quoins; stone foundation in random coursed, hammer dressed rubble capped by a cut and tooled stone plinth; low-pitch gable roof clad in asphalt shingles with a boxed cornice and decorated frieze; two large wooden parapets with crenellated cornices flanking the tower; recessed tympanum with carved diamond pattern decoration placed above the entryway; heavy limestone arch featuring carved voussoirs of alternating length above the tympanum; aureole window with a heavy limestone surrounds and interlacing glazing bars; dentils, block modillions and a blind lancet window with interlacing glazing bars found near the top of the tower; aluminum steeple with surrounding four finials; replacement of the original copper steeple; pointed arch triple light Gothic window opening with flamboyant style tracery on the north (rear) facade; built along the historic Portage Road and has a historical connection to the Mackenzie Rebellion of 1837-1838; attended by various significant people both local (e.g. Laura Secord) and international (e.g. King Edward VII); continues to serve the community as it has for over 150 years

properties.Name: Stamford Green
properties.Statement: Once the residence of Captain Robert Dee, his sold  the lands to the Stamford Green Board of Trustees for $1000 provided that no building be erected, no trees planted, and no fence erected.  There are several monuments on the property.
properties.Attributes: Its rarity, being an open greenspace that has not been significantly changed or planted on since the early 20th century; association with prominent early settlers in Stamford Township- Captain Robert Dee and his son Dr. John Dee; historic role in community events and militia musters; site of visit in 1860 by Prince of Wales, later King Edward VII, large open landscape in contrast to surrounding development on Portage Rd; proximity to Portage Rd, a major transportation link between Niagara Falls and Queenston; preservation as an open greenspace

properties.Name: First Bampfield House
properties.Statement: The house (c. 1860) is a unique variant of the Regency style with a perfectly square plan, tall limestone block walls and a high raised basement. The basement was dynamited out of the underlying bedrock and built in the earth and rubble technique without mortar. The attached rear porch shed and roof dormers are later additions. Built by local lumber merchant John Merrall, this was the first home of the Bampfield family on their arrival in Clifton in 1860. James Bampfield operated the Great Western restaurant in the east wing of the railroad station. The house was also reputedly used as a brothel for many years earlier in this century.
properties.Attributes: Roof clad in asphalt shingles with hipped-roof dormers on all facades; single storey with a symmetrical five bay façade; square building with a plain limestone exterior laid in broken course; high basement with a rubble stone foundation; Italianate style elements including the low-hipped roof, rounded openings and brackets; modillion brackets under the broad eaves; a centred round headed arched opening leads to a recessed front door; double front door contains glass panels with a transom above; rounded arched window openings with 8 light sash have splayed limestone voussoirs; rectangular 2 over 1 window with plain surrounds in basement level; small square opening containing coloured glass window with moulded surrounds; modern enclosed porch on the west facade of the structure; associated with the Bampfield family, who were involved in the social and economic development of the City

properties.Name: Former All Saints Anglican Church
properties.Statement: William Hay a notable designer of many churches in Toronto and Upper Canada. He was an architect of Romantic leanings and incorporated a number of Gothic features into his buildings. All Saints (c. 1856)  has elements  of an English rural parish church, with a massive square tower and narrow Gothic lancet windows. The builder was William Russell a local contractor who also owned and operated a brewery in Drummondville. The Church has a small chancel at the east end. The windows have finished limestone surrounds and small lip sills. The land for All Saints Church was donated by Lieutenant-General John Murray's wife. Lieutenant Murray was a shareholder in the unsuccessful City of the Falls Company. Murray street was named after him. The Reverend William Leeming, was the first rector of All Saints. However it was his curate the Rev Charles Leycester Ingles who oversaw the building of the Church.
properties.Attributes: Interior:  23 memorial stained glass windows; rood screen which separates the chancel from the nave; exposed wooden rafters, characteristic of William Hays' designs; stone baptismal font by George Armitage; 12 rows of pews on the north side and 17 rows of pews on the south side divided by a centre aisle.  Exterior: The style, form, massing and orientation of the rectilinear plan; steep roof pitch; low bell tower with 1500lb Meneeley Bell; surrounding cemetery; Indigenous limestone construction; simple lancet windows; simplicity of architectural detailing; buttresses, pointed window arches, carved hoodmolds which terminate in foliate drip stops.

properties.Name: Buckley House
properties.Statement: The styling of the Buckley House (c.1891) reflects the American "stick style" movement of the late 19th century, with decorative wood elements represent the underlying structure. Its unique details include the bay window set at a 45 degree angle to the corner and pent roofs with curved brackets over the bay window and the main entrance. The house's date of construction is recorded in four terra cotta blocks installed in the fireplace chimney.  The original owner was Morton Havelock Buckley.  The Buckleys were the most prominent commercial family in Clifton during the 1870's and 80's, operating a variety of shops. Morton Buckley (1857-1925) owned a successful furniture store later operated by his son Ernest for many years. The house remained in the Buckley family until 1982.

properties.Name: Timothy Hixon House
properties.Statement: The main part of the house (c. 1870) was built in the picturesque Gothic style, perhaps as early as 1833. It has double brick walls, a steeply pitched central gable and a front porch with decorative scrolling. a kitchen wing on the west side was built of brick in 1937 and has since been covered with vinyl siding. Timothy Hixon, the original owner, and his brothers produced bricks in a yard immediately west of the house; these were shipped along the river to Chippawa or Port Robinson. The house has been in the Lambert family since 1903.  There may have been another house located at 9037 Chippawa Creek Rd which has been demolished.  This house would have belonged to a Miss Marie Hixon (perhaps a sister or other family member) a portion of that house was said to have been built before 1812.

properties.Name: Willoughby-Sauer Church
properties.Statement: The upper facade and walls are decorated with corbelled brickwork. The windows maintain the original Florentine style tracery. A rear addition was built in 1949 and the original gabled roof vestibule at the front was replaced with the present flat roofed version in 1964. This church  (c. 1883) was the second owned by the Evangelical congregation; it replaced the earlier 1863 log Church. The land was donated by W.H. Sauer, an early settler of the township and one of the church's first converts and built by George Burger. The cemetery to the north of the building has served the local community since the mid 19th century. The Church is now occupied by the Steinberg Organ Co.

properties.Name: Francis Sherriff House
properties.Statement: This house (c. 1894) is an excellent example of a Queen Anne Revival style with an asymmetrical form, deep porch, complicated roof line including gables, dormers and a turret. The house exterior is brick with decorative cedar shingles being used on the turret and in the gables. The 3 part window in the front gable is an adaptation of the Palladian style. The central section has a round headed window. the large wrap-around porch has Tuscan style columns that rest on a brick base topped with a square stone cap. The house was built for Francis Sherriff in 1894 by Jacob Lovell for a cost of $4000.00. Francis Sherriff and Thomas Bright were the two young Torontonians who started the "Niagara Falls wine  company" (Brights Wines) in Toronto in 1874. They moved to Niagara Falls in 1890 to be closer to their major source of grapes.

properties.Name: VIA Railway Station
properties.Statement: Constructed (c. 1879) in the Gothic Revival style favoured for rail depots of the Victorian age, it exhibits a hipped gable roof, decorative brick banding and limestone door and window accents. Originally installed in the gable ends were carved bargeboards. The interior was renovated in 1951 and the east wing partially demolished in 1967. Positioned beside the International Railway bridge, this was the busiest and most prestigious terminal of the Great Western and Grand Trunk railroads. It serviced the growing tourist trade, and was a popular social centre with a restaurant in the east wing. It was federally designated in 1995 and locally by City Council in 1999.
properties.Attributes: Excellent example of Gothic Revival style; two storey central section flanked by one storey wings; red brick laid in Flemish bond; decorative band separating the first and second levels; three courses of corbelled brick at the window openings; a corbelled brick frieze where the wall meets the eaves; projected brick quoins on each corner; variations of a Gothic arch, with limestone springblocks, keystone and sills; original 1 over 1 wood sash and glazing pattern; central gable bull's eye opening; several wood two panel doors; jerkin head roof with clipped gable ends; gables were originally decorated with ginger bread trim; paired wooden eave brackets with chamfered edges and trefoil pattern; tongue and groove soffit; connected to the history of the Village of Elgin; connected to the development of tourism, economic and population growth in the City

properties.Name: Ellis-Taylor House
properties.Statement: This house (c. 1894) exhibits various elements of the Queen Anne Revival style: patterned brick on the round corner tower, a curved verandah and tripartite Palladian gable windows. Other distinguishing features are the carved front doors with glass panels and a large round arched parlour window equipped with a stained glass transom. The house was constructed by Fred W. Ellis and owned by Arthur Park Ellis. The Ellis family acquired many of the lots south of Morrison Street and later sold/developed them. In 1899, it was purchased at auction by merchant Frank Taylor and remained his home until 1945. From 1953-65, it served as accounting offices for the Niagara Falls Board of Education.

properties.Name: Solomon Miller House
properties.Statement: Built in the unique octagonal style by George Burger (c. 1889), it has an eight sided hip roof, a doorway in every other wall and a summer kitchen attached to its northeast side. Under the summer kitchen is the original cistern which is still in working order. The window and doorway arches are built with yellow brick. The rooms inside the house are constructed around a central core which contains the stairways.  Solomon Miller (1842-1926), a wealthy and respected farmer, was a member of one of the first families to have settled in Willoughby township. His home, built for his wife Catherine shortly after their marriage, was one of the first brick houses in the area.

properties.Statement: Associated with the Loretto Academy.  The East Lawn and iron gate along the property line are its historical features.

properties.Name: Egerton Morden House
properties.Statement: This fine example of a board and batten house (c. 1876) borrows from the Italianate and Stickley styles, associated with the picturesque movement in the second half of the nineteenth century in Upper Canada.  It has an irregular "l" shaped plan with a one story kitchen and bedroom extension to the rear. It has patterned wood shingles and ornamental roof brackets. This house has been relocated from Dorchester Road to Corwin Ave. Egerton Ryerson Morden who lived in and built this house operated a successful nursery on 10 acres of land that surrounded his home. He specialized in small fruit plants and ornamental trees. He was a well respected horticulturalist and was active in municipal affairs serving on the Stamford Township Council. His son James C Morden was one of the areas most respected educators and historians.
properties.Attributes: Rear example of a board and batten residence; combination of Italianate and late nineteen century styles arranged in the Picturesque manner; set close to the ground well back from Dorchester Road in a treed setting; it is ell shaped--the front is arranged in a three sided bay; window sashes are predominately 1 pane over 1 but in some four over 4 panes exist; small window facing street from rear extension features a pent roof; around window openings the trim as ear mould details; between first and second floor windows in the gable facing the street and the wall above the front door are decorative wood shingles; there are decorative sunburst pattern brackets under the eaves of the front bay.

properties.Name: Danner Sherk House
properties.Statement: An example of the early Georgian-Loyalist style, (c.1810)  the house features massive stone walls covered with stucco. Low pitched gable roof and an interior plan arranged around a central hall. The rear wing, built c. 1820, housed a loom room on the upper floor. The original end chimneys have been removed and the multipaned sash windows have been replaced with modern casement windows. During the War of 1812, the house served as a British HQ and Commissary. It was owned by the Ebenezer Community (1847-55), Ultrich Strickler, the Sherk family (1855-1926) and by J.A. MacTaggart, tourism promoter and originator of Tussaud's Wax Museum on Clifton Hill.
properties.Attributes: Two storeys with an asymmetrical four bay façade; an example of Loyalist style, popular in the first quarter of the 19th century; constructed of a coursed rubble limestone with stucco finish; limestone foundation; rear wing constructed of dressed limestone blocks; low-pitched gable roof with cedar shingles; two single inset chimneys on both ends; front entrance with side lights and wood paneling in the door recess; gable pediment above the entire doorcase; rectangular window openings, three on the first storey and four on the second storey on the east (front) facade; north and south facades have two rectangular window openings on both the first and second storey; two square window openings in the gable ends on both facades; windows on the north side of the house are noticeably narrower than those on   the facade and south wall; connected to several key figures in the township history including Ultrich Stickler, Joseph Danner, Elias Sherk and John MacTaggart; linked historically to the development of the Willoughby Township, the War of 1812, and the Rebellion of 1837-1838

properties.Name: Bank of Montreal Building
properties.Statement: Built by the Merchants Bank of Canada (c. 1918-1920) , it was designed by Ralph K. Shepard who designed many banks across Canada.  The Merchants Bank operated from 1920-1929.  In 1929, the Bank of Montreal moved into the building where they remain today.

properties.Name: John Thomson Jr House
properties.Statement: The house's original styling would have been typically  Loyalist with 1 1/2 storeys and a low pitched gable roof without dormers. The present roof, with decorative wood detailing on the gable ends and shed dormers, and the front portico were probably added in the 1890's. The original stone walls are 3 feet thick. It was built by John Thomson Jr., son of John Thomson who owned the Whirlpool Farm. The house (c. 1825) sat in the midst of a large farm which occupied  most of Stamford Township Lot #108. A small portion in the rear dating around 1800, was supposedly the site of the first meeting of the Masons in the Stamford area.
properties.Attributes: Loyalist style two storey building with a symmetrical five bay façade; constructed of solid limestone blocks laid in even course with a quarry faced finish; stone foundation; high-pitch gable roof incorporating three shed dormers; decorative brackets and wood mouldings beneath the eaves; gable ends with a projected entablature supported by brackets and fan-like wood detailing; large central dormer with brackets beneath the eaves, a closed pediment with a fantail tympanum, and paired rectangular 2 over 2 sash windows with a shared wood mullion between; shed dormers with a 2 over 2 sash window, fan-like ornamental siding and brackets beneath the eaves; four 2 over 2 sash windows with plain trim and louvered shutters on the west (front) facade; hip-roofed portico supported by four Doric order columns with decorative brackets; front door features pilasters, recessed panels and sidelights; three inset brick chimneys; associated with the Thomson family--developers of Portage Road and Stamford Township

properties.Name: Battle Ground Hotel Museum & Fralick's Tavern
properties.Statement: In 1836, the land was purchased by Adam Fralick to construct a tavern.  It offered lodging, food and drink to travelers--benefiting from it's location on the Historic Lundy's Lane Battlefield and the adjacent Battlefield observation tower.  The hotel was owned by the Fralick family until it was sold to James A. Lowell in 1898.  Ruth Evelyn Redmond donated the land and building to the City in 1996.  The building is consistent with Classical Revival style and features a seven bay facade, the primary gable contains a recessed centre porch and forms a classical temple facade supported by two Doric order columns.  There are three points of entry reflecting the building's use as an Inn.
properties.Attributes: Primary gable with eave returns typical of the Classical Revival style; central front door with simple square profiles featuring 6 raised panels, two pilasters with heavy cornice, and a plain stepped entablature; temple façade form, characteristic of Classical Revival style, supported by two Doric order columns; symmetrical facade with a seven-bay arrangement providing a balanced appearance; 12 over 12, 12 over 8 and 8 over 8 sash window arrangement and fixed louvered shutters; refurbished clapboard siding; rubble stone foundation; cornice gutters restored on second floor roof; cedar shingles used in the primary gable and south facing gable end; retained interior features in the east parlour, including a fireplace with mantle, baseboards and trim and panels beneath the windows; original banister and sponge painted walls; association with Adam Fralick, owner of the house and key player in the development of early tourism in the Niagara Region; proximity to other properties designated for their heritage value in relation to the Battle.

properties.Name: James Ingles House
properties.Statement: This house (c. 1855) is an example of Cottage Gothic, a picturesque style popular in the mid 19th century.  It has a central peaked gothic gable and a jerkinhead roof. The windows have simple wooden drip caps. The central door opening has a transom and side lights. The house and the property (1 acre) was purchased by John Chamberlaynne Ingles in 1886. John and his wife Helen sold the house and property in 1910. The house underwent extensive renovations in the 1920's. Georgian style paneling was added to the hall and living room.
properties.Attributes: One and half storey Gothic Revival Cottage style; symmetrical three bay façade; limestone foundation; stucco exterior; Jerkin head roof style with central peaked gable and clipped  gable ends; open porch supported by paired columns, topped by a broken pediment and an arched ceiling; central front entrance, with sidelights, transom, recessed panels; 2 over 2 sash windows with plain trim and drip molds; 1 over 1 sash window with plain trim and drip mold located in the central gable; connection to the City's Anglican community and the history of All Saint's Church; connection to the Ingles family, prominent figures in the City's development.

properties.Name: Battle of Lundy's Lane National Historic Site of Canada
properties.Statement:
The Battle of Lundy’s Lane National Historic Site of Canada is located in Niagara Falls, Ontario. The battle occurred on July 25, 1814 on what was a rise of clear farmland surrounded by an orchard and forest, situated upon Lundy’s Lane. The location of the site is now marked by a plaque located within Drummond Hill Cemetery. Lundy’s Lane was the site of a major battle between the British and American forces in which the Americans, who were advancing after the Battle of Chippewa, attacked the British defensive position that they had taken up. Following a bitterly contested engagement, the
Americans withdrew. The six-hour long battle was one of the bloodiest battles of the War of 1812 and marked the end of American offensive action in Upper Canada. Official recognition refers to a parcel of land in the City of Niagara Falls that is roughly four-blocks square and encompasses the
site of the battle.
properties.Attributes: Four blocks encompassing the battle site.

properties.Name: Detenbeck Home
properties.Statement: The only surviving example of an Ebenezer Society house, (c.1850) it was constructed of large logs and boards, joined by the mortise and tenon method, with clapboard exterior. The eave returns, boxed cornice roof trim and the windows with their plain, wide trim are standard details of Ebenezer construction.  The Ebenezers ( the community of true inspiration) originated in Germany. They lived here as a self-sufficient community from 1849 until 1859, when they moved on to Amana, Iowa. Their property was bought by Martin Kabel and was referred to as "Kabeltown" for a number of years later.

properties.Name: Davey Automotive
properties.Statement: Formerly John Evans' Inn (c. 1820). The hotel dates from around 1846 and was considered to be first rate.  The widow of John Evans' ran the hotel for many years after her husband's death. It later became Reid's Grocers (at the ground level).  It bears the symmetrical proportions of a Loyalist house.  It is a two storey frame house with five bays and a medium pitched gable roof.  It still has one of its chimneys.

properties.Name: Dr. James McGarry House
properties.Statement: This substantial home (c. 1896) with its corner tower, pressed brick and limestone exterior, and irregular roofline has changed little in the course of a century. The large Neoclassical front porch features rounded columns, frieze and a decorated closed pediment.  It was designed by John Clark and built by Frank Nugent. A surgery was added to the rear of the house in 1905. The house served as both the home and office of Dr. James (and Louisa) McGarry, and later that of his son, pediatrician Dr. Howard McGarry. Between them, the house was the center of medical care for countless families in Niagara Falls over the course of nearly ninety years.

properties.Name: Ray Corry Bond House
properties.Statement: This vernacular style shingled cottage was built sometime in the early 1900's (c. 1907) and holds a prominent position on the street.  It provides the historical backdrop for the life of Ray Corry Bond. This was the home of Ray Corry Laura Bond, who was an exceptionally active community worker and supporter.  She did extensive research into Chippawa's past that resulted in a book entitled PENINSULA VILLAGE.  Mrs. Bond was born in Stamford Township in 1885 and graduated from Trinity College and the Ontario Teacher's College.  She married James R. Bond in 1914.  The couple lived in this house  ‘the Riverview Cottage’ which had been Ray's home since 1907.  Mrs. Bond was honoured with a Canada Centennial Medal in 1967.  She lived in this cottage until her death in 1970.

properties.Name: St. Mary's Ukrainian Catholic Church
properties.Statement: Completed in 1988, the Church was designed by Stecura and Timothy Bullock was the craftsman builder.  The design was based on Ukrainian Church architecture rom 1000 years ago.  It incorporates a central dome and a square cross plan with four arms.  It is built from white pine timbers that came from the Tomogami region of Northern Ontario.  There are not many windows--which is traditional as church were used as a sanctuary from attacks by Mongol tribes.  The main source of light is from the dome and a central Byzantine chandelier that was imported from Greece.

properties.Name: Logan Block
properties.Statement: The building (c. 1907) was designed by William Nichols and built by Alonzo Robertson; they would later collaborate on the Carnegie Library. It is representative of the early 20th century commercial building with its refined Classical styling and practical structure. The upper facade has remained essentially unaltered.  The block was constructed for John Logan (1862-1955), a prosperous downtown merchant and respected civic leader for 67 years. His decision to relocate his dry goods store from Erie Avenue to Queen Street affirmed the position of Queen as the new axis of downtown commerce.

properties.Name: Henry Spence House
properties.Statement: The main part of the house (c. 1885) built by Henry Spence has a square stone foundation; attached to the northeast corner is a rear wing with a gable roof. Among its details are the semielliptical transom over the front door, a large three part parlour window and a bay window on the east wall. The front porch with its square tapering support columns is likely an early 20th century addition.  Henry Spence (1809-1894) was a successful mason and builder of the Drummondville area. Born in England, he emigrated to Canada with his family in 1817. He had acquired a significant amount of property over the years in what is now central Drummondville. He also owned a homestead farm on township lot 161 south of present day Dunn street from 1854-1885.
